title: Common Cold
content: Symptoms may include sneezing, sore throat, mild fever, runny nose, and cough. General precautions include rest, warm fluids, and monitoring for worsening symptoms such as difficulty breathing or persistent high fever.

title: Seasonal Flu
content: Flu often presents with fever, body aches, fatigue, headache, sore throat, and cough. Mild cases benefit from hydration, rest, and fever monitoring. Seek urgent care for breathing difficulty, confusion, blue lips, or dehydration.

title: Strep Throat
content: Strep throat can involve sore throat, fever, painful swallowing, and swollen glands. Medical testing is often required to confirm the diagnosis. Encourage doctor evaluation if symptoms are significant or persistent.

title: Migraine
content: Possible signs include throbbing headache, nausea, sensitivity to light, and sensitivity to sound. Hydration, rest in a dark room, and routine OTC pain relief may help some people if previously tolerated.

title: Food Poisoning
content: Food poisoning can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach cramps, and weakness. The main precautions are hydration, bland foods, and emergency evaluation if severe dehydration, blood in stool, or persistent vomiting occurs.

title: Allergic Rhinitis
content: Symptoms may include sneezing, itchy eyes, congestion, and runny nose. General steps include avoiding triggers, using clean indoor air, and considering common OTC antihistamines if already known to be safe for the user.

title: Paracetamol
content: Paracetamol or acetaminophen is commonly used for fever and mild pain. Remind users to follow label directions, avoid exceeding package limits, and avoid duplicate combination medicines that also contain acetaminophen.

title: Ibuprofen
content: Ibuprofen may help mild pain, headache, or fever for some adults. Avoid suggesting it for people with stomach ulcers, kidney issues, NSAID allergy, or certain pregnancy situations. Advise label-based dosing only.

title: Oral Rehydration
content: Oral rehydration solutions can support hydration during mild vomiting or diarrhea. Encourage small frequent sips and urgent evaluation if the patient cannot keep fluids down or shows dehydration warning signs.

title: Saline Nasal Spray
content: Saline nasal spray may help with congestion and nasal dryness. It is general supportive care and does not replace medical evaluation for severe infection symptoms.

title: Fever Care
content: Rest, adequate fluids, light meals, and temperature monitoring are common supportive measures. High fever, confusion, seizures, or breathing problems need urgent medical care.

title: Sore Throat Care
content: Warm fluids, salt-water gargles, hydration, and rest may offer relief. Seek care for drooling, severe swelling, breathing trouble, or symptoms that persist.

title: Headache Care
content: Hydration, rest, sleep, and reducing bright light may help some headaches. Emergency care is recommended for sudden severe headache, neurological deficits, or head injury.

title: Chest Pain Warning
content: Chest pain, chest pressure, pain radiating to the jaw or arm, fainting, or shortness of breath may represent an emergency. The assistant must advise immediate medical attention.

title: Breathing Difficulty Warning
content: Shortness of breath, wheezing with distress, blue lips, or inability to speak in full sentences can indicate emergency danger. Advise immediate medical attention.

title: Stroke Warning
content: Face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, confusion, or sudden one-sided numbness are emergency stroke warning signs. Advise immediate medical attention immediately.

title: Asthma
content: Symptoms include shortness of breath, chest tightness, wheezing, and coughing. Avoid known triggers and use prescribed inhalers. Seek emergency care for severe breathlessness.

title: Gastroenteritis
content: Often called stomach flu. Symptoms are watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and sometimes fever. The most important precaution is replacing lost fluids and electrolytes to prevent dehydration.

title: Hypertension
content: High blood pressure often has no symptoms but can cause headaches, shortness of breath, or nosebleeds in severe cases. Lifestyle changes include reducing sodium, regular exercise, and stress management.

title: Type 2 Diabetes
content: Symptoms can include increased thirst, frequent urination, increased hunger, unintended weight loss, fatigue, and blurred vision. Management includes blood sugar monitoring, a healthy diet, and physical activity.

title: Antihistamines
content: Antihistamines like Cetirizine or Loratadine can relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching, runny nose, and watery eyes. Warn users about potential drowsiness with some types and advise following label directions.

title: Antacids
content: Antacids can neutralize stomach acid and relieve heartburn, indigestion, and upset stomach. They are for short-term use. Advise users to see a doctor if symptoms persist for more than 2 weeks.

title: Dehydration Care
content: Drink plenty of fluids, such as water, clear broths, or oral rehydration solutions. Avoid caffeine and alcohol. Seek medical help if unable to keep fluids down or if experiencing severe dizziness or confusion.

title: Severe Bleeding
content: Continuous bleeding that doesn't stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure, or blood that is spurting, is a medical emergency. Advise immediate medical attention.
